description: We are four Electrical and Electronics Engineering students. Abdullah, Sinem, and Sıla focus on electronics, embedded systems, and prototyping, while Ertürk focuses on signals and signal processing. We previously worked together in METUSTARS, where we developed an indoor hospital navigation system and finished with a placement. We want to build a hands-on project combining hardware, signals, coding, and prototyping.
summary:
MOONPOINT is an interactive lunar mission-planning tool designed to make landing-site evaluation at the Moon’s south pole easier and more intuitive. Users can select a candidate landing site and mission date, then explore the relative positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon through an interactive visual interface.

The application translates ephemeris data into practical mission information such as sunlight availability, direct-to-Earth communication opportunities, and operational time windows. Instead of requiring users to interpret complex astronomical tables, MOONPOINT presents this information visually and allows different locations and dates to be evaluated quickly.

Our goal is to bridge the gap between accurate space-science data and an accessible decision-support tool that can be useful for mission planning, education, and public exploration.
details:
MOONPOINT was developed as a browser-based mission-planning application for evaluating candidate lunar south-pole landing sites.

The user selects a landing location and mission date, after which MOONPOINT processes astronomical data to determine the relative geometry of the Sun and Earth as observed from the selected lunar location. The results are transformed into mission-oriented indicators including sunlight availability, direct-to-Earth communication availability, and operational visibility windows.

A major focus of the project is visualization. Instead of presenting mission planners with raw ephemeris tables, MOONPOINT uses an interactive 3D environment and graphical mission information to show where the selected landing site is located and how the Sun and Earth appear relative to it. This allows users to understand the effect of location and time on lunar operations much more quickly.

NASA/JPL Horizons data is used as the astronomical basis for Sun and Earth position calculations. Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and LOLA resources were also studied for lunar topography and landing-site context. The application was developed as a web-based system and deployed publicly using Render.

MOONPOINT is designed not to replace professional mission-analysis tools, but to make their underlying information more accessible and intuitive. Its intended impact is to support rapid comparison of lunar landing scenarios while also providing an educational way to explore the engineering constraints of missions to the lunar south pole.
